検索エンジンは、文書を「索引(インデックス、検索しやすい形に整理された一覧のようなもの)」に入れる前にチャンク分割や整形をするが、この整形の仕方自体をAIエージェントに探索させて自動最適化する論文が出ていた(https://arxiv[.]org/html/2607.18603v1)。

検索の精度を上げたいとき、普通は検索に使うAIモデル(文章の意味を数値に変換する埋め込みモデルや、候補の並び順を調整するリランカーなど)そのものを改良しようとする。この研究「AutoIndex」が狙うのはその手前の工程。検索アルゴリズム自体(BM25というキーワード検索の定番手法)は完全に固定したまま、文書をどう切り分けて索引に入れるかを決めるプログラムだけをAIに書かせて磨き込む。

仕組みは2つのAIエージェントの往復。Analysisエージェントが今の索引で検索に失敗している具体例を実際に読みに行って原因を診断し、Codeエージェントがその診断をもとに前処理コードを書き直す。書き直すたびに索引を作り直して精度を測り、良くなった版だけ採用、を5回繰り返す。

医療、法律、コード検索など性質の異なる8種類のタスクで試したところ、全タスクで検索の再現率(Recall@100、正解の文書を上位100件以内に含められた割合)が改善し、平均+8.4%、最も伸びたタスクでは+30.5%だった。

中身が具体的で面白い。「あの映画のタイトル何だっけ」的な曖昧な記憶からの検索タスクでは、AIは文書を分割せず、あらすじ部分を3回、キャスト欄を2回繰り返して1つの塊に埋め込むという力技を自力で発見していた。別のタスクでは文書中の数式表記が検索のノイズになっていると見抜き、数式の多い文書だけを狙って除去するコードを書いていた。以前の試行で消しすぎて成績を落とした反省を踏まえた設計になっている点も芸が細かい。

BM25専用に学習したはずのこの前処理プログラムを、埋め込みベクトルで類似度を測る密検索にそのまま流用しても、あるタスクでRecall@100が0.74から0.87まで上がったらしく、汎用性もありそうな結果になっている。

反復探索にしたのが効いていて、1回きりの書き換えだと8タスク中3つしか改善しなかったらしい。検索精度を上げたいとき、モデルより先に「索引の作り方」を疑う余地は普通にありそう。

Memory Caching (arXiv 2602.24281) caches memory checkpoints per segment and retrieves across them at read time. The write rule doesn't change. It's a read-side fix and it works

I tested the write side and it failed

Memoir is four weight tiers on different update intervals. W0 every forward pass, W1 gated per segment, W2 slow consolidation, W3 frozen. A ponder loop with learned halting sits on top. The claim was that every ponder step writes into the fast weights

12 seeds on the hard task. Coupled 0.5203, read-only 0.6557, paired t 3.23, read-only wins 10 of 12. A 960-step control closed it to 1.0000 both arms, so it's a learning-speed penalty at fixed budget, not a capability ceiling. Confound I'm not burying: the coupled arm writes 7x more often

Their segment checkpoint and my W1 are the same instinct. They grew the read, I moved the write. The read side won

The latest report from the National Drug Early Warning System should concern every parent, educator and public-health professional.

NDEWS recorded 16,335 suspected nonfatal overdose-related EMS encounters involving MDMA, commonly sold as Ecstasy or Molly, between January 1, 2023, and June 30, 2026.

More than half occurred in Southern states:

• South: 8,955
• West: 2,705
• Midwest: 2,557
• Northeast: 2,118

But the numbers tell only part of the story.

NDEWS is also warning about counterfeit products, drugs sold as MDMA being mixed with other substances, and the possibility of illicit fentanyl appearing in this unpredictable supply.

As a father who lost my 16-year-old son Daniel to a counterfeit pill, I cannot say this strongly enough: you cannot trust the appearance, color, shape or name of an illicit pill. What someone believes is Molly or Ecstasy may contain something entirely different, and one pill can be enough to cause irreversible harm or even death.

We must keep educating young people with honest, current information. The illicit drug supply continues to change, and our prevention efforts must change with it.

https://www.mcdonaldhopkins.com/insights/news/fbi-renews-warning-on-ai-generated-deepfakes?utm_content=383326845&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter&hss_channel=tw-63105555

"Seeing is believing" is no more relevant
▫️Techniques like diffusion models, 3D NeRFs, and zero shot voice cloning have rendered synthetic media indistinguishable from reality. While this unlocks massive creative potential, it presents critical enterprise risks; from executive impersonation to biometric bypass.
▫️The path forward requires shifting from simple detection to cryptographic media provenance (C2PA).
🔸Will detection tools ever catch up or are we stuck in a Zero Trust digital environment ❓

AI can now mimic a person's face and voice with startling accuracy. Deepfakes can make anyone appear to do or say anything. A familiar face or voice no longer guarantees authenticity.

Be cautious. Check the source.

#ThinkBeforeYouShare

Deepfake rapid response units are facing algorithmic attacks.

Automated audio verification is being used to check spectral patterns, voice consistency, AI manipulation, and source reliability.

#DeepfakeDetection #RapidResponse #AudioVerification #CrisisCommunication
The AI Deception Machine: Deepfakes, Chatbots, and the New Frontier of Senior Fraud https://twitter.com/i/broadcasts/1jxXggNErWeJZ

We talk about deepfakes as if they're the frontier of synthetic media

They're not

Synthetic text at scale — AI-generated comment sections, fake op-eds, manufactured "expert consensus" — is already deployed and largely undetected

The face gets the headlines

The words do the work

Reducing online impersonation scams is like a math equation.  

Read how government + banking, social media and telecom industry collaboration = fewer scams.

https://bpi.com/impersonation/

TikTok is testing an opt-in deepfake detection tool. Creators verify their identity through Jumio by uploading a government ID and a live selfie, then TikTok scans the platform for AI-generated content matching their face.

Opt-in is a good start, and built-in detection helps the creators using it, especially after Meta's Muse Image showed opt-out sets the wrong default.

The bigger need is cross-platform protection. A creator protected on TikTok or YouTube can still have their likeness appear elsewhere, and no single platform can watch the wider internet on its own.

Verification is another area still evolving. Uploading an ID to a third party adds friction and a new custodian to trust. Tools like PersonaShield use face-based verification instead, where the likeness itself becomes the credential, keeping the trust closer to the person being protected.

TikTok's tool is a meaningful step, but the next layer is protection that runs across every platform, not just where someone posts.

posts.text:
The heroes just come home from defeating the greatest evil and oppressive super power of their age, and what do they find in the Shire? A washed out wizard and a king's advisor assaulting their village, despite having been defeated in the second book.

Thats the equivalent of Goku and his friends just beating Frieza on Namek in DBZ, then coming home to find Ginyu and Guldo holding their families hostage and have to fight them.

Or Superman just beating Darkside, saving the universe, and returning to Metropolis to find Granny Goodness has taken over his city.

Or Luke Skywalker just beating Vader and escaping the Death Star explosion, only to find Admiral Piette has taken Endor and needs to deal with him to finish the movie.

Or Odysseus returning fron his voyage to his palace, only to find the Cyclops Polyphemus' brother has taken up residence and wants a piece of him...

Should I go on?

By far my favoruite example is in Legend of the Galactic Heroes.

The use of spreadable particles that ignite when a gun is fired in their vacinity, forces boarding crews to equip themselves in armor and wield axes.

It also helps that it's very well choreographed.

If you take Invincible as an example. It has examples of good and bad of this. With the bad, after the whole series hypes up how unstoppable viltrumites are they have random bugs make him struggle which takes you out of the story because the core conflict is around fighting

I unironically love Frieren and Goblin Slayer for these exact reasons, among other things. 

I still remember a "discussion" with a dude that went something like "Is goblin slayer really about killing just goblins and are they really just evil and not simply misunderstood." 

This line of questions went cyclically for an hour where me and a bunch of other friends were like, "Yes, and yes." The dude revisited his initial questions several times, hence the length of time. That's where we're at with the, "actually they're misunderstood" reveal and how expected it is.

To say nothing of how self-indulgent it feels in this day and age when a movie centered on a dead trope is trotted out to beat its corpse over the head like its a present day offender, e.g. the movie Damsel.

The Warrior

“This is a weapon of terror. It’s made to intimidate the enemy.”
“This is a weapon of war. Its purpose is to kill the enemy.”

The absolutely greatest and and most effective military lampshading scene in the history of Science Fiction. It’s lamp-shading because sometimes what you’re writing is a big fucking lamp that’s being misconstrued.

In a single scene you eliminated all accusations of the “Imperial Stormtrooper Marksmanship Academy” for the Jaffa, showing that they miss a lot becasue their primary weapon sucked at being a weapon, and all their tech is hobbled by its religious dual-purpose. Simultaneously you justified the Air Force wiping the floor with a multi-planetary empire that stole technology and didn’t earn its place because it only beat up on the defenseless. We have military doctrine, logistics, and professional planning and execution taken from a history of evolving warfare. The Threat are cosplayers who steal technology and turn it all into the tools of narcissism.

It’s one of my absolutely favorite episodes on the strength of the writing that properly dusts off and paints five seasons of framing in hunter orange so everyone can see it clearly.  If I was a prop collector I’d put that fucking thing in my living room.

Started and dropped: The Warrior Princess and Barbarian King.

Couldn't make it 5 minuets. The barbarians, with their weak technology and metal working can cleave through the steel of the empire's armored troops in a single sword swing and their cheap iron helmets deflect bullets. The fight looks obviously CG. Soldiers wait their turn to fight, standing around awkwardly until the script calls for them to die. Both sides immediately stop fighting whenever someone important talks. There is no weight to any movement or action.

I could eat a bowl of Alphabet Soup and shit a better script for a fight scene.

Have I been ruined by good anime?

Something I’ve noticed about the vocal audience on here is that they operate off of basic enemy/ally distinction.

If it’s an “enemy”, aka someone in the protagonist’s way, it’s ok if the “hero” kills them. Because they’re the hero! They have their reasons.

If they’re with the “hero”, then they’re an ally and anything that happens to them is a tragedy to be focused on.

People are gonna argue that Eleven here is justified because these men were part of the military, which experimented on her, and they were in her way, so ergo, it’s ok for her to kill them because she deserves that catharsis. The military are the bad guys, so it’s ok, it’s fine, don’t think about it, this is storytelling.

However, if any of Eleven’s friends were to be killed in this manner, completely overwhelmed while they were getting in the way of someone else, then it’ll be a travesty and “too brutal”.

“It’s not that deep, bruh.”

This is more addressing a wider issue with how people miss any sort of nuance whatsoever. It’s why if a hero has a “no kill” or “minimize death” rule there is an increasing amount of people that just go “why shouldn’t these people die? They’re the enemy!” Because media has allowed things to degrade to such a manner.

If she has the power to so effortlessly snap their necks and also make a guy shoot himself, she could have just as easily knocked them out. This indicates a level of nuance to her portrayal to where she is conscious of all life, not just those with her. I am also aware that they were trying to kidnap her and what was happening with the pregnant women. Even then, she had the drop on them, she could have shown restraint for the higher ideal of a heroic figure.

Were they active shooting her in this scene and she had to put them down? Completely fair, but these basic portrayals do a lot in shaping the overall morality of the characters we see.

Especially when we get takes like this who just go “wooo yeah! This is so satisfying!” As the “hero” demonstrates no restraint and just kills people in her way.

If I was going to write this scene to make Eleven not come off as so careless about life, I would have had the soldiers actively shooting at her as she takes cover/stop the bullets so she is forced to used lethal force to defend herself. This doesn’t change the outcome, but now it changes the portrayal. Everyone gets a more nuanced portrayal, and people can still clap like seals.

I again await everyone telling me that I’m thinking too much about this and I should just shut my brain off to enjoy things.

Spider-Man Brand New Day (2026) review:

I enjoyed it overall even though I had some issues with some things that happened in the movie. Fight scenes were cool. Scenes with Peter and Frank were nice. I genuinely loved #Alpha. Barring a few shots in the climax & few dialogues, I had a great time watching it.

The second half is just as engaging as the first. The emotional and character driven conversations between Alia Bhatt, Sharvari, and Anil Kapoor are surprisingly well-written and leave a strong impact. Alia's acting, attitude, screen presence, and intensity stand out throughout the film. From her entry to the climax, she completely owns the screen and delivers one of her most powerful performances.

As Sita and Durga, Alia & Sharvari share excellent chemistry. Their hand-to-hand combat sequence is, in my opinion, the best I've ever seen in Indian cinema. It feels raw, intense, and beautifully choreographed. Almost every hand to hand fight and action sequence is top-notch and keeps you invested.

The only action scene that didn't completely work for me was Kabir's cameo fight. That said, Kabir's screen presence is absolutely phenomenal. The moment he appears, he completely commands the screen with his charisma, swag, and aura. Even with limited screen time, he leaves a lasting impact and reminds you why he's one of the most iconic characters in the YRF Spy Universe. 

The Sita vs. Fateh hand-to-hand combat sequence is another major highlight and is executed brilliantly.

The songs are okay overall, but Haniya Ve and Massacre are visually stunning. Both Alia and Sharvari look gorgeous, and I genuinely couldn't take my eyes off Alia in both the songs.

Sharvari as Durga looks gorgeous throughout the film and has a strong screen presence. She performs well in both the emotional and action scenes.

Anil Kapoor as Kaul delivers a solid performance. His scenes with Alia and Sharvari are well-executed & add emotional weight to the story.

Bobby Deol as Fateh is a convincing antagonist with a strong screen presence. His Haryanvi accent worked well for me and suited the character.

Overall, I had a fantastic time with the film. It's an entertaining action thriller with strong performances, stylish action, and plenty of crowd pleasing moments. It's not a perfect movie, but it's absolutely worth watching if you're looking for a fun big-screen experience.

I'll definitely be watching it again, especially for my sunshine, @aliaa08 ♥️

The Brady Handgun Violence Prevention Act of 1993 (Public Law 103-159), commonly called the Brady Act or Brady Bill, required federal background checks for firearm purchases from licensed dealers and established an interim five-business-day waiting period for handguns.
It is named for James Brady, the White House press secretary who was severely wounded and left partially paralyzed in the March 30, 1981, assassination attempt on President Ronald Reagan by John Hinckley Jr. Brady and his wife Sarah led a long public campaign for the measure.
Key details
• Sponsor and passage: Introduced in the House by Rep. Charles E. Schumer (D-NY). After years of prior attempts, it passed the House (238-189) and Senate in November 1993. President Bill Clinton signed it into law on November 30, 1993; it took effect on February 28, 1994.
• Interim provisions (handguns only, until late 1998): Federally licensed dealers, manufacturers, or importers could not transfer a handgun to an unlicensed person without first receiving a statement of eligibility, verifying identity, notifying the chief law enforcement officer in the buyer’s area of residence, and waiting five business days (or less if cleared sooner). Local officials were to make a reasonable effort to check for disqualifying records. Exceptions existed (e.g., certain permits or threats). Records for approved transfers were to be destroyed.
• National Instant Criminal Background Check System (NICS): The law directed the Attorney General to create a national instant check system within five years so dealers could quickly verify whether a transfer of any firearm would violate federal or state law. NICS (run by the FBI) went online on November 30, 1998, after which the five-day waiting period ended. Dealers contact NICS; if no prohibiting information is found (or after three business days with no response), the transfer can proceed.
• Other elements: It funded improvements to state criminal records systems, included provisions on multiple handgun purchases (reporting to local police), and contained some reforms related to federal firearms licenses. It applied only to sales by federally licensed dealers (private sales were not covered federally).
Context and impact
The Act built on the Gun Control Act of 1968 by ending the previous “honor system” in which buyers simply certified they were not prohibited persons. Prohibited categories include felons, fugitives, certain domestic violence offenders, illegal aliens, and those adjudicated mentally defective, among others. Background checks have blocked millions of attempted purchases by prohibited persons over the decades.
A 1997 Supreme Court decision (Printz v. United States) held that the federal government could not compel state/local officials to conduct the interim background checks, but the overall framework and NICS continued.
This remains the primary federal law requiring background checks for purchases from licensed firearms dealers.
